assessments.fundamentals: HDB is a commercial bank with legacy property activities. H1 2026 standalone net profit was EGP 9.924bn, up 11.2%; NIM declined to 15.3% from 17.2%, while credit-loss impairment rose 144.4%. CAR 41.7%, NPL ratio 4.2% and coverage 173.2% provide stronger evidence than generic debt/equity [results]. Consolidated parent profit was EGP 10.760bn and reported H1 EPS EGP 10.13 on weighted average 1.0626bn shares [statement]. Snapshot P/E 5.76/PB 2.45/ROE 49.66% must be judged against sustainable bank ROE, funding, loan quality and rate sensitivity; do not extrapolate exceptional returns or mix standalone and consolidated EPS. No fair value model is asserted.

assessments.catalysts: The 11 August release reports the new CEO appointment and continued banking expansion [results]. Those are disclosed developments, not proof of an imminent rerating. Next results should test margin compression against loan growth and provisioning. The issuer regulatory page returned no readable announcement list, and the dividend page stops at 2021 [actions, dividends]; neither supports a claim that no later actions exist.
assessments.risks: Moderate-to-high: interest-rate repricing, credit costs, property exposure and a correcting share price. NUCA is listed at 29.81%, RELACO about 10%, REMCO 9.84%, Misr Life 9.09%, Misr Insurance 8.29%, Social Housing Fund 7.41% and Endowment Authority 5.03% [owners]. No individual listed holder has majority ownership. Presentation share data is labelled 31 December 2025 and uses an older 531.3m share count [presentation]; June accounts show EGP 10.626bn capital after a EGP 5.313bn increase [statement]. Exact effective/ex-action dates and current register must be confirmed. Prior-20-observation median daily volume 225,852 shares; median close-times-volume turnover proxy EGP 23856906.35. assessments.entryConditions: No entry now. Monitor a new reversal near 102–104 that preserves 102.03 support, or a confirmed reclaim/retest of 112.40 with renewed volume. Those are alternative future hypotheses, not active signals; after either, re-evaluate structural stop, available resistance and adjustment history. Do not chase merely because the screen calls valuation cheap. At the reference close 107.79, an illustrative stop 99.53 and nearest-resistance target 112.40 imply EGP 8.26 per-share downside (7.66%) versus EGP 4.61 upside (4.28%), gross reward/risk 0.56. A hypothetical 0.50% round-trip cost scenario yields EGP 8.7990 loss and 0.46 reward/risk. Costs are a stress assumption, not known broker charges. This is diagnostic math, not an approved entry or guaranteed loss cap.
